data.title: String generator puzzle
data.solution:
# The algorithm below is similar to the "merge" step of mergesort,
# except applied to strings whose characters are not lexicographically ordered.

# The number of strings
n = int(input())

# An array of strings
s = [list(input()) for _ in range(n)]

# The result string
r = ""

# Check if any string still has characters
while any(s):
    # Find the index corresponding to string with the smallest first character
    # Inner part: Get indices of non-empty strings
    # Outer part: Compare first element of each non-empty string to find smallest
    i = min((i for i in range(n) if s[i]), key=lambda i: s[i][0])

    # Remove first character from the string and add it to results
    r += s[i].pop(0)

# Print the results
print(r)
data.statement:
Create a string from input strings [[s]] by repeatedly selecting the smallest current first character among the strings, using ASCII order. Continue until all characters have been used.

Test cases will not require tie-breaking.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Create a string from input strings s by repeatedly selecting the smallest current first character among the strings, using ASCII order. Continue until all characters have been used.

Test cases will not require tie-breaking.
Input
Line 1: An integer n, the number of input strings.
Next n lines: A string s.
Output
A single line containing the generated string.
Constraints
1 ≤ n ≤ 16
1 ≤ length(s) ≤ 32

For simplicity:
• All input strings in a test cases have the same length.
• Each input string contains only letters, either all uppercase or all lowercase.
• Test cases never mix upper and lower characters.
Example
Input
2
ac
bd
Output
abcd
